codeReview.summary: The implementation covers the feature requirements well — delimiter injection stripping, instruction injection neutralization, test suite, and threat model documentation are all present and the 27 tests pass. However, there are two bugs in the sanitizeBookmarkText() function that represent correctness issues: (1) the closing </superuser> tag is not filtered (only the opening tag is), and (2) the regex for collapsing 3+ consecutive closing braces is incorrectly written — it matches '}{' followed by 3+ '{' chars instead of 3+ '}' chars. Additionally, HTML comments (<!-- -->) are not stripped by the generic tag filter, though this is lower severity.

issues.description: Only the opening <superuser> tag is replaced with [filtered], but the closing </superuser> tag is not. The code comment on line 89-90 explicitly acknowledges this: 'NOTE: <superuser> must be checked BEFORE generic tag stripping below, because the generic pattern would strip it first, leaving only </superuser> unmatched.' Despite noting the problem, it was not fixed. Result: sanitizeBookmarkText('<superuser>admin</superuser>') produces '[filtered]admin</superuser>' — the closing tag leaks through, which could be exploited. The generic tag filter at line 107 matches <[a-zA-Z][^>]*> which doesn't match </superuser> because it starts with </ not a letter. Fix: add a separate .replace(/<\/superuser>/gi, '[filtered]') after the opening tag replace, or change the opening tag regex to /<\/?superuser>/gi.

The regex /\}{{3,}/g is intended to collapse 3+ consecutive closing braces, but the pattern actually matches a literal '}' followed by 3+ '{' characters then '}'. The correct regex should be /\}{3,}/g (matching 3+ consecutive '}'). Current behavior: sanitizeBookmarkText('}}}}}}') (6 closing braces) produces '}}}' instead of the intended '}' — it only collapses pairs via the /\}\}/g regex on line 117. The tests don't catch this because they only test {{ }} patterns (double braces), not 3+ closing braces. Fix: change line 115 from .replace(/\}{{3,}/g, '}') to .replace(/\}{3,}/g, '}').

HTML comments like <!-- ... --> are not stripped by the generic tag filter. The regex /<[a-zA-Z][^>]*>/g requires the tag name to start with a letter, so <!-- ... --> is not matched. While HTML comments in bookmark text are unlikely to be a practical injection vector (LLMs generally ignore them), it's an inconsistency in the tag-stripping approach. The safe tag allowlist approach could be extended to also strip HTML comments with .replace(/<!--[\s\S]*?-->/g, '').

The test 'collapses duplicate closing braces' only tests double braces (}}) but not 3+ closing braces (}}}). This means the buggy regex on line 115 of the source file is not effectively tested. A test like assert.equal(sanitizeBookmarkText('}}}').length, 1) would have caught the bug. Similarly, no test covers the /\}{{3,}/g regex's actual behavior with inputs like '}{{{{'''.

summary: The feature implementation is mostly sound — it adds comprehensive prompt injection mitigations (delimiter stripping, instruction injection patterns, JSON structural injection, truncation) and a thorough 27-test suite. The threat model documentation in JSDoc is well-written. However, two bugs cause a FAIL: (1) the closing </superuser> tag is not filtered despite the code comment acknowledging it should be, and (2) the regex for collapsing 3+ consecutive closing braces is incorrectly written (\}{{3,} matches '}{' + 3+ '{' + '}' instead of 3+ '}'). Both bugs mean the sanitization is incomplete in edge cases that the feature description explicitly calls out ('stronger neutralization... add a test suite covering injection patterns'). A non-blocking concern is that HTML comments bypass the generic tag stripper.
